curriculum.heading: Curriculum & Learning Structure
curriculum.description: Designed for an AI-native era, combining deep computer science foundations with independent, hands-on software engineering.

principles.title: Learning to Learn
principles.desc: The capacity to master new languages, tools, and frameworks independently without waiting for a classroom lecture.
principles.meaning: Self-directed learning: discovering how to read documentation, debug errors, and acquire technical skills on demand.
principles.whyItMatters: Technologies and frameworks change rapidly. Engineers who learn independently remain future-proof.
principles.example: Adopting a newly released AI library or cloud SDK and building a working prototype within 48 hours.

principles.title: Learning to Think
principles.desc: Reasoning from first principles, questioning assumptions, and validating AI-generated code with independent human judgement.
principles.meaning: Analytical reasoning: breaking down complex problems into clear algorithmic logic and system architecture.
principles.whyItMatters: AI copilots can write syntax, but engineers must evaluate architecture, security, and scalability.
principles.example: Identifying hidden race conditions or edge-case bottlenecks in code generated by an AI assistant.

principles.title: Learning to Do
principles.desc: Experiential software engineering where students build, debug, and ship production software daily.
principles.meaning: Hands-on execution: replacing passive blackboard lectures with 100% active studio building.
principles.whyItMatters: Real engineering intuition comes from building and breaking systems, not memorizing slides.
principles.example: Designing real microservices, setting up CI/CD pipelines, and deploying to cloud infrastructure.

eligibility.heading: Eligibility & Admission Process
eligibility.description: Clear guidelines on qualifying undergraduate backgrounds, application evaluation, and admission milestones.

criteria.title: Undergraduate Qualification
criteria.desc: Bachelor's degree in Engineering or Technology (B.Tech / B.E.) or Master's degree in Computer Science, IT, Computer Applications (MCA), or Mathematics from a recognized university.

criteria.title: Engineering Disciplines
criteria.desc: Graduates from both CS/IT and non-CS engineering branches (such as ECE, EEE, Mechanical, Civil, etc.) are eligible to apply. Foundation tracks are designed to build essential computing fundamentals.

criteria.title: Final-Year Students
criteria.desc: Students appearing in their final semester/year of undergraduate studies are eligible to apply provisionally, subject to completing all graduation requirements before programme commencement.

criteria.title: Academic Marks & Cutoffs
criteria.desc: Official minimum percentage or CGPA cutoff criteria will be formally specified in the upcoming admission circular. No assumptions or speculative cutoffs are enforced.

criteria.title: Prerequisites
criteria.desc: A sound background in higher secondary/undergraduate mathematics and a genuine aptitude for problem solving and programming are expected.

criteria.title: Work Experience
criteria.desc: Both fresh graduates and candidates with professional software or engineering experience are welcome to apply.

admissionProcess.title: Online Application
admissionProcess.desc: Candidates submit the MSIT application form with required academic credentials, mark sheets, and statement of interest.

admissionProcess.title: Screening / Entrance Evaluation
admissionProcess.desc: Shortlisted candidates undergo the prescribed admission evaluation assessing problem solving, programming logic, and analytical aptitude.

admissionProcess.title: Interview / Interaction
admissionProcess.desc: Candidates may be invited for an interaction to assess preparation, academic mindset, motivation, and suitability for the programme.

admissionProcess.title: Admission Offer
admissionProcess.desc: Selected candidates receive formal admission offers with instructions for fee payment, document verification, and enrolment.

eligibility.disclaimer: The admission process, evaluation format, and schedule for the January 2027 cohort will be confirmed in the formal notification. Dates and procedures are subject to institutional approval.

questions.question: What is MSIT?
questions.answer: MSIT is the Master of Science in Information Technology postgraduate programme offered by the Consortium of Higher Learning, anchored at IIIT Hyderabad. Founded over 25 years ago by Turing Award laureate Prof. Raj Reddy, the programme emphasizes hands-on learning, practical engineering, and close mentorship.

questions.question: What is different about the revamped MSIT?
questions.answer: The revamped MSIT is being designed as an AI-native programme, centred on three principles: Learning to Learn, Learning to Think, and Learning to Do. It combines academic computing education with substantial industry co-op experience, AI-assisted learning, venture building, and continuous learning improvements through CETLS.

questions.question: When will the next cohort begin?
questions.answer: The next cohort of the revamped MSIT programme is scheduled to begin in January 2027. Official admission announcements will be released shortly.

questions.question: Will AI be part of the curriculum?
questions.answer: Yes. AI will be both an area of core technical study and an integral tool used across the learning environment. Students will learn how to build AI systems, use modern AI tools effectively, and critically evaluate AI outputs using independent human judgement.

questions.question: Is MSIT primarily lecture-based?
questions.answer: No. MSIT has historically emphasized experiential learning and learning-by-doing through project studios, active coding, and real problem solving rather than relying primarily on conventional classroom lectures.

questions.question: What is the role of CETLS?
questions.answer: MSIT serves as a living laboratory for the Centre for Educational Technology and Learning Sciences (CETLS) at IIIT Hyderabad. Curriculum, pedagogy, student assessments, and mentoring interventions are continuously studied and improved using evidence-based cognitive science.

questions.question: What is the industry co-op structure?
questions.answer: The redesigned programme plans for students to spend approximately half their programme duration working on genuine corporate engineering problems under the guidance of industry practitioners and faculty mentors.

questions.question: What is the Venture Studio?
questions.answer: The Venture Studio provides builder-oriented students an opportunity to take a problem or idea from inception towards a potential product or startup venture, gaining exposure to the startup and early-stage investment ecosystem.

questions.question: What are the eligibility criteria for admissions?
questions.answer: Candidates with undergraduate degrees in Engineering/Technology (B.Tech/B.E.) or Master's degrees in computing disciplines (MCA, M.Sc in CS/IT/Maths) are eligible to apply. Specific minimum percentage/CGPA cutoffs will be published in the official admission notification.

questions.question: Can final-year undergraduate students apply?
questions.answer: Yes. Students currently completing their final year/semester of undergraduate degree requirements are eligible to apply provisionally, provided they complete all graduation requirements before commencement.

questions.question: Can students from non-computer science engineering branches apply?
questions.answer: Yes. Graduates from other engineering disciplines (ECE, EEE, Mechanical, etc.) are considered. Foundational immersion modules are structured into the initial curriculum to establish strong programming and systems fundamentals.

questions.question: What is the programme fee structure?
questions.answer: The detailed fee structure for tuition, registration, caution deposits, and other institutional charges for the January 2027 cohort will be formally published in the official admission circular.

questions.question: Are education loans available for MSIT?
questions.answer: Yes. Admitted students of IIIT Hyderabad master's programmes are typically eligible for education loans through major nationalized and scheduled banks. The institute provides official admission offer documentation and fee estimates to facilitate loan processing.

questions.question: Is hostel accommodation available?
questions.answer: Hostel and residential arrangements for the January 2027 cohort are being finalized in line with institutional capacity and will be confirmed in the formal admission notification.
